record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Geometric dilation of planar point sets
record.original_question: Determine the smallest real number t such that every finite planar point set has geometric dilation at most t, where geometric dilation takes the supremum over all pairs of points lying on the graph’s edges or vertices rather than only over original input vertices.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 20. What is the smallest value of t such that every finite set of points in the plane has geometric dilation at most t? It is known that (1 + 10−11)π/2 ≤ t ≤ 1.678.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ and a connected planar embedded graph $G$ whose vertex set contains $P$ (edges are rectifiable Jordan arcs in the plane), define the geometric dilation of $G$ by
$$\delta(G)=\sup_{p\neq q}\frac{d_G(p,q)}{\|p-q\|},$$
where the supremum is taken over all pairs of distinct points $p,q$ that lie on the vertices or edges of $G$ (not only on the vertices of $G$), $d_G(p,q)$ denotes the length of a shortest path in $G$ between $p$ and $q$ measured along the embedded edges, and $\|p-q\|$ denotes the Euclidean distance. Define the geometric dilation of the point set $P$ by
$$\delta(P)=\inf_{G\supseteq P}\delta(G),$$
where the infimum ranges over all such planar graphs $G$ containing $P$ among its vertices.

Determine the exact value of
$$t^* = \sup\{\delta(P) : P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\text{ finite}\},$$
i.e. the smallest real number $t$ such that every finite planar point set admits an embedding into a planar graph of geometric dilation at most $t$. It is known that
$$\left(1+10^{-11}\right)\frac{\pi}{2}\le t^*\le 1.678.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The best known bounds remain (1+10^{-11})π/2 ≤ t* ≤ 1.678, due to work by Ebbers-Baumann, Grüne, Klein and Dumitrescu–Ebbers-Baumann–Grüne–Klein–Rote. No closed-form value of t* has been established; the gap between the lower and upper bounds remains open.

status_evidence.title: On the geometric dilation of closed curves, graphs, and point sets
status_evidence.snippet: Every finite point set is contained in a planar graph whose geometric dilation is at most 1.678, and some require at least π/2.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the upper bound 1.678 and lower bound π/2 for the dilation constant t*.

status_evidence.title: Improved lower bound on the geometric dilation of point sets
status_evidence.snippet: Improves the lower bound to δ ≥ (1+10^{-11})π/2.
status_evidence.claim: Current best lower bound (1+10^{-11})π/2 with the upper bound 1.678 still standing; exact value remains unknown.
